title: 十五分钟卖光了  (Sold Out in Fifteen Minutes)

segments.t: At the bustling café counter, Mei slices golden tarts onto white plates as fast as Qing and Peng can carry trays out to the tables. Listen to the whole scene first.
大树底下的四号桌，要两杯薄荷茶、三块柠檬挞！
马上好！志鹏，把热茶壶端到靠窗的角落桌去！
二号桌说，这层杏仁挞底是梧桐巷最好吃的点心！
告诉二号桌，秘诀是我星期三收的两个厨房徒弟！
小美，第四盘柠檬挞还剩几块？
你数一数：一、二、三——四十块十五分钟就卖剩三块了！
幸好你多烤了两盘热乎乎的肉桂卷以防万一！
快听——屋子里刚安静下来！有人在敲谱架！
十号院的邻居把他的小提琴盒带进九号房了！
干净盘子先放五分钟，你们俩快到门口来听！
最后那三块柠檬挞，留给宋老师、老陈和周经理！
解下围裙吧——星期五六点到了！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
大树底下的四号桌，要两杯薄荷茶、三块柠檬挞！

'Two mint teas and three lemon tarts for table four under the tree!' In a café, Mandarin orders name the table first as the topic—"table four under the big tree"—and then call out everything they want after "yao".
马上好！志鹏，把热茶壶端到靠窗的角落桌去！

'Coming right up! Peng, take the hot teapot to the corner window table!' "Mashang hao!" is the classic kitchen call for "coming right up!", and "kao chuang"—"leaning near the window"—is the exact chunk to ask for a window table.
二号桌说，这层杏仁挞底是梧桐巷最好吃的点心！
'Table two says this almond crust is the best pastry on Wutong Lane!' Look how lovingly "dianxin" names a pastry: literally "touch the heart"—a little treat meant to warm your spirits with tea.
告诉二号桌，秘诀是我星期三收的两个厨房徒弟！

'Tell table two the secret was my two kitchen apprentices on Wednesday!' "Mijue" means a craftsperson's secret knack, and "shou tudi"—"taking in apprentices"—comes straight from traditional Chinese kitchens and workshops.
小美，第四盘柠檬挞还剩几块？
'How many slices of lemon tart are left on tray four, Mei?' Unlike "duoshao" for big open numbers, "ji" asks "how many" when you already suspect only a handful remain on the tray.
你数一数：一、二、三——四十块十五分钟就卖剩三块了！

'Count them: one, two, three—out of forty slices, down to three in fifteen minutes!' Watch "shu" in "shu yi shu": read with a dipping third tone it means "to count", whereas the exact same character in fourth tone gives "shuzi", "number".
幸好你多烤了两盘热乎乎的肉桂卷以防万一！

'Good thing you baked two extra trays of warm cinnamon rolls just in case!' Slipping "duo", "more", right before "bake" means "bake extra". And "yifang wanyi" literally says "to guard against one in ten thousand"—"just in case".
快听——屋子里刚安静下来！有人在敲谱架！
'Listen—the room just went quiet! Someone is tapping a music stand!' Adding "xialai", "come down", after "quiet" captures chatter settling into a hush, just like English "quieted down".
十号院的邻居把他的小提琴盒带进九号房了！

'Our neighbour from number ten brought his violin case inside Room Nine!' Mandarin names the violin "xiaotiqin", literally "small hand-carried stringed instrument"—alongside "big hand-carried instrument" for the cello.
干净盘子先放五分钟，你们俩快到门口来听！

'Leave the clean plates for five minutes, both of you—come listen at the door!' "Nimen lia" is the warm spoken shortcut for "both of you"; because "lia" already fuses "two" and its counter into one syllable, you never add "ge" after it.
最后那三块柠檬挞，留给宋老师、老陈和周经理！
'Save those last three slices of tart for Teacher Song, Chen, and Manager Zhou!' "Liugei" joins "keep" with "for", giving you a handy everyday chunk whenever you save dessert or a seat for a friend.
解下围裙吧——星期五六点到了！
'Aprons off—it is six o'clock on Friday!' "Weiqun" literally means "wrap-skirt"—an apron—and "jie xia" pictures untying the strings to slip it off.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
大树底下的四号桌，要两杯薄荷茶、三块柠檬挞！
马上好！志鹏，把热茶壶端到靠窗的角落桌去！
二号桌说，这层杏仁挞底是梧桐巷最好吃的点心！
告诉二号桌，秘诀是我星期三收的两个厨房徒弟！
小美，第四盘柠檬挞还剩几块？
你数一数：一、二、三——四十块十五分钟就卖剩三块了！
幸好你多烤了两盘热乎乎的肉桂卷以防万一！
快听——屋子里刚安静下来！有人在敲谱架！
十号院的邻居把他的小提琴盒带进九号房了！
干净盘子先放五分钟，你们俩快到门口来听！
最后那三块柠檬挞，留给宋老师、老陈和周经理！
解下围裙吧——星期五六点到了！
All thirty-seven slices of tart vanish in fifteen minutes, and the whole courtyard falls quiet as six o'clock arrives. See you next time.
